pr_title: conf-parse: make config_parse_many() optionally save 'struct stat' for each file
pr_comments: This works as a resolution for #21113

@poettering Thank you for you review. I'd like to keep the function name at least in this PR. I am planning the Hashmap introduced in this PR make also used in PID1. So, I will re-consider the function name if it can be reused and moved to e.g. stat-util.[ch]. Merging.

comments:
```
eth0: found matching network '/etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network'.
eth0: Re-configuring with /etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network
```
Is the file path expected?
Yeah, that's the file that was used for the configs above

Do you update the .network file in place with an editor or script?
Or, there are two (or more) .network files, and one is `00-bmc-eth0.network` with the `[Address]` section, and another is the .network file without `[Address]` section which is named something alphanumerically later, e.g. `10-bmc-eth0-without-address.network`?

I cannot reproduce the issue with the current git HEAD. IIRC, we have not changed anything about the logic of reloading .network files since v249.

Rewriting it is scripted, but I can reproduce it on the command line pretty trivially. I am overwriting the file with the same name. The process is roughly
```
cat <file contents 1> >/etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network
# Ensure the service picks up the first set of contents correctly
systemctl restart systemd-networkd
cat <file contents 2> >/etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network
networkctl reload
networkctl reconfigure eth0
```

 and then it still acts as though the contents never changed and stays in the state of <file contents 1>
Hm, the timestamp (mtime) of the file is updated? Currently, networkd detects whether each .network file is updated or not by using its timestamp.

```
root@jrxi22-nfd01:~# cat eth0-1 >/etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network 
root@jrxi22-nfd01:~# networkctl reconfigure eth0
root@jrxi22-nfd01:~# networkctl reload
root@jrxi22-nfd01:~# networkctl reconfigure eth0
root@jrxi22-nfd01:~# date
Thu Jan  1 00:06:29 UTC 1970
root@jrxi22-nfd01:~# ls -la /etc/systemd/network
drwxr-xr-x    2 root     root             0 Jan  1 00:00 .
drwxr-xr-x    1 root     root             0 Jan  1 00:00 ..
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root           236 Jan  1 00:06 00-bmc-eth0.network
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root           108 Jan  1 00:00 00-bmc-eth1.network
```
One more question. If you restart (not reload) systemd-networkd.service after `00-bmc-eth0.network` is updated, then the address is configured?

Yeah, if I restart systemd-networkd it does pick up the file. It looks like when I turn off debugging and send the logs back to the journal it is obviously not seeing the file update? I recall seeing something printed in the past if the file was updated.

> It looks like when I turn off debugging and send the logs back to the journal it is obviously not seeing the file update?

`eth0: Re-configuring with /etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network` This should be logged with LOG_INFO.
And we have no log message related to file update.

```
touch /etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network
networkctl reload
journalctl -u systemd-networkd -o short-monotonic --no-hostname -f
[  427.154337] systemd[1]: Started Network Configuration.
[  427.366061] systemd-networkd[2640]: Failed to stat network namespace, ignoring: No such file or directory
[  427.401739] systemd-networkd[2640]: Failed to stat network namespace, ignoring: No such file or directory
[  723.631128] systemd-networkd[2640]: Failed to stat network namespace, ignoring: No such file or directory
```

One more question. Do you have any drop-in configs for `00-bmc-eth0.network`, e.g. `00-bmc-eth0.network.d/foo.conf` under `/etc/systemd/network`, `/run/systemd/network/`, or `/usr/lib/systemd/network`?
Yes, `/lib/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network.d/gbmc-ncsi.conf`

If I touch this file, networkd will correctly identify that it needs to reload the config and print `eth0: Re-configuring with /etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network`. However, even with `networkctl reload` and `networkctl reconfigure eth0` it doesn't apply the new addresses or routes.
Nevermind, ignore my previous statement about it missing the addresses. I had the old file in place. If i correctly update the network file and touch all of the drop-ins doing a reload works now.

> Yes, /lib/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network.d/gbmc-ncsi.conf

I guess this drop-in file has the newest timestamp compared with the main .network file (or other drop-in files). And your system seems to not have clock battery. So, even if you edit or touch the main .network file, `networkd` mistakenly considered no files are updated. And discard newly loaded files.
Thus, even if you explicitly trigger `network reconfigure eth0`, the address is not assigned to the network.

Thank you for answering many questions. I hope now I get the root of the issue. I will prep a patch. Please wait for a while.

Note. An example workaround for the issue is, when you edit the main .network file (or even a drop-in config), touch all relevant drop-in configs to make update mtime (when you edit a drop-in, then touch its main .network file and other drop-ins). Please try that.
I hope PR #21114 fixes your issue. If possible, please test it. Thank you.

The title of the fix tracks how I would have suggested solving the problem. I'll test it soon and let you know.

You are right about the timestamps on the drop-in file. For some reason I thought yocto was setting all of the root filesystem contents to a deterministic timestamp but apparently not. It has a timestamp that is recent, obviously newer than jan 1 1970. Apparently I'm used to how nixos achieves package purity and forgot our yocto images don't do something similar (it's probably an options we should turn on if it exists).

@yuwata unrelated question, what's the correct way to regenerate link local addresses if an interface mac changes? Right now if I change the mac address I would need to bounce the interface to have it regenerate. AFAICT reload / reconfigure / renew / forcerenew do not handle this.
How about once down the interface before reload/reconfigure, by `ip link set dev eth0 down` or `networkctl down eth0`?

Yeah, that’s what we have been doing. I had hoped there was something to avoid the time spent renegotiating link status when flapping the link.

I should test deleting the address and reconfiguring.

I am not sure about all interface type support that, but at least dummy interface can regenerate an IPv6 LL address by once removing the IPv6 LL address and set new MAC address. That is, calling `ip addr del dev eth0 IPv6LLADDR` before reload/reconfigure may work at least some kinds of network interface.

review_comments: is "equal" really the right name for this? maybe "_unmodified"?

For me, "equal" sounds suitable for "stats", and "unmodified" sounds suitable for "file" (or "path").
So, I prefer "equal" here. But not strong opinion. If you or others prefer "unmodified", then I will rename it.
